subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput decision follow-up

Alex — great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we can move toward a clear recommendation between Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity (or Private VPC if it becomes necessary).

What we heard from you on the call:
- Use case: real-time fraud scoring for payments (inline scoring on checkout).
- Typical request: ~300-400 tokens total per request (prompt + model output).
- Baseline throughput: target ~50-60 reqs/sec steady state; peaks up to ~120 reqs/sec for bursts (minutes-long).
- Latency targets: p95 target ~150ms or lower; p99 ideally <250ms but you said anything above ~300ms is a hard no for checkout flows.
- Data posture: PCI-scope — leaning toward provider-hosted but open to Dedicated/Private if it simplifies compliance scope.

Initial guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest path to production and easiest onboarding. For many customers with bursty workloads and average throughput in the 50-80 RPS range, Hosted is sufficient when you accept higher variability at p99 and rely on our edge routing and caching.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need predictable p99/p95 SLOs for checkout latency, or if you need sustained high concurrency with aggressive tail-latency targets. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, pinned model versions, and the ability to tune batching/cache policies for deterministic behavior.
- Private VPC/on-prem: usually reserved for customers with strict egress/KMS requirements or full data residency needs. Based on our call it sounds like Dedicated will likely be the sweet spot unless your compliance team insists on VPC-only.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the sustained baseline (50-60 RPS) vs. the length and frequency of the 120 RPS bursts? (minutes, hours, daily?)
2) If you confirm bursts are minutes-long, we can run a short Dedicated sizing exercise to show expected p95/p99 latencies and provide a monthly quote. Marissa — can you prepare a quick sizing worksheet and expected latency envelope for the workload (attaching a draft sizing to start).
3) If you'd like to move quickly we can spin a Hosted pilot with traffic mirroring for 2 weeks to validate quality and avg latency while the Dedicated sizing is worked in parallel.

Attachments: finpay-initial-sizing-draft.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally once you send the peak profile.

—Dylan

Dylan — thanks for the write-up and for the call. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Baseline is closer to 60 RPS during business hours. Peaks to ~120 RPS happen 4-6 times per day and typically last 3-8 minutes (spikes tied to batch release windows).
- Latency: our product SLA requires p95 <= 150ms for checkout flows; p99 ideally <= 200-250ms. Anything that regularly produces p99 > 300ms will be a blocker.
- Compliance: PCI team is OK with vendor-hosted if we can get strong logging/audit and guaranteed data partitioning (no model training on customer data). Dedicated or VPC is preferable if it materially improves predictability.

For the pricing side — can you provide a ballpark for a Dedicated reserved pool that handles sustained 60 RPS and 120 RPS short bursts? Also would like the expected p95/p99 numbers for the baseline and burst scenarios (include assumptions on batching and sequence length).

Appreciate it — want to get this into our vendor shortlist by end of next week.

—Alex Turner
CTO, FinPay
alex.turner@finpay.io

- p95 <= 150ms; p99 goal <= 200-250ms; p99 > 300ms is rejectable.
- Compliance: vendor-hosted acceptable if we can provide audit logs / data partition guarantees; but they prefer Dedicated if it improves predictability.

Can you:
1) Confirm a recommended Dedicated config (GPU count / type, autoscale policy, burst buffer) that meets p95/p99 targets for both baseline and burst (assume 350 tokens average).
2) Call out any tradeoffs where Hosted might still be preferable (time to production, cost delta) and provide a ballpark monthly pricing range for the Dedicated pool + ops support.
3) Prep a one-pager we can send to Alex with expected p95/p99 numbers, cost delta, and pilot plan.

I’ve attached the draft sizing spreadsheet — feel free to update. Neha — once Marissa confirms, please include a rough quote we can share. FinPay needs vendor shortlist by EOW.

Thanks — Dylan

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput decision follow-up

Thanks — I updated the sizing draft and ran a quick internal sketch for expected latencies. High-level notes:
- Assumptions: model = LLM-X (optimized), avg sequence = 350 tokens, request size distribution as provided.
- Recommended Dedicated configuration: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) with an autoscale headroom to add 2 GPUs on sustained >80 RPS for >5 min.
- Expected performance (approx): baseline 60 RPS -> p95 ~120ms, p99 ~180-220ms (depends on batching hit-rate); burst to 120 RPS with autoscale -> p95 ~140-170ms, p99 ~220-260ms.
- Notes: Dedicated with KV/prefix caching tuned for FinPay (high cache hit expected) is the main lever to tighten tail latency. Hosted can hit avg p95 numbers but will show wider p99 variance during bursts.
- Ballpark pricing: Dedicated reserved pool (4 GPUs + 2 GPU burst headroom) + standard support = $45k-65k / month depending on commit term and telemetry retention. Exact quote to be provided by Neha.

I attached the updated sizing: dedicated-sla-latency-estimates.pdf and updated the spreadsheet. If we want to shorten pilot time, I recommend running a 1-week Dedicated smoke test (mirroring a 10% sample of traffic) and a parallel 2-week Hosted pilot for quality verification.

I’ll prepare the one-pager for Alex with the numbers above and the pilot plan; sending draft by EOD.

—Marissa
